host_cli.help: Server health: load, memory, disk, network (item 22 of the SSH menu)
host_cli.help.health: The light, the findings with advice, the checks and the light network probes
host_cli.help.set: Server health settings: on or off, light probes, check points, the level of the bot’s notifications
host_cli.help.probes_hint: The line “you can turn on light probes” for the result of an update (empty when not needed)
host_cli.help.on: Turn the server health check on
host_cli.help.off: Turn the server health check off (the light says “off”, no health notifications)
host_cli.help.probes: Light network probes: on or off (off — not a single packet goes out)
host_cli.help.anchors: Check points separated by commas — public IPv4 or IPv6 addresses in digits, up to 5; default — the default points
host_cli.help.push_level: The bot’s health notifications: crit — alarms only, warn — warnings too
host_cli.off_hint: To turn it on — kaskadctl host set --on
host_cli.off_hint_screen: To turn it on — 2 on this screen
host_cli.probes.off: Light network probes: off. To turn them on — kaskadctl host set --probes on
host_cli.probes.off_screen: Light network probes: off. To turn them on — 2 on this screen
host_cli.probes.idle: The probes run only while the gateway works (item 17 of the SSH menu)
host_cli.probes.idle_legacy: The probes run only while the gateway works, and the gateway needs the nftables engine (items 16 and 17 of the SSH menu)
host_cli.read_fail: Could not read the server health: {error}
host_cli.set.nothing: Say what to change: --on or --off, --probes on|off, --anchors, --push-level crit|warn, --bench-retry on|off, --dev-threshold 5…30, --dev-spread on|off
host_cli.set.on_off_both: --on and --off together are not allowed: choose one
host_cli.set.bad_level: The notification level is crit or warn (given “{value}”)
host_cli.set.no_anchors: Give the check points separated by commas, or default — back to the default points
host_cli.set.bad_anchor: “{addr}” can’t be a check point: a public IPv4 or IPv6 address in digits is needed — no name, no %, not private, not reserved, not multicast
host_cli.set.own_anchor: “{addr}” is an address of this server: it can’t be a check point
host_cli.set.name_anchor: “{addr}” is an address of the name {host} (this server’s client address): it can’t be a check point
host_cli.set.no_ipv6: The server has no IPv6: the point {addr} will be “not checked”
host_cli.set.enabled_on: The server health check is on.
host_cli.set.enabled_off: The server health check is off: the light says “off”, no health notifications.
host_cli.set.probes_on: Light probes are on — the collector takes them within 10 s, the first measurements come in under a minute.
host_cli.set.probes_on_idle: Light probes are on — they start once the gateway works (item 17 of the SSH menu).
host_cli.set.probes_on_disabled: Light probes are on, but the server health check is off — the probes start once it is turned on: kaskadctl host set --on.
host_cli.set.probes_on_legacy: Light probes are on — they start once the server moves to nftables (item 16 of the SSH menu) and the gateway works (item 17).
host_cli.set.probes_off: Light probes are off — they stop within 10 s, no more packets go out.
host_cli.set.level_crit: The bot’s health notifications: alarms only.
host_cli.set.level_warn: The bot’s health notifications: alarms and warnings.
host_cli.set.soon: The collector picks up the changes within 10 s.
host_cli.set.same: Nothing changed: it is set this way already.
host_cli.help.bench_schedule: The schedule of the server checks
host_cli.help.bench_apply: apply — set the timer of the schedule again
host_cli.bench.what: Say what to do: schedule apply
host_cli.help.bench_retry: Check again in 1–2 h when a link drops sharply: on or off
host_cli.help.dev_threshold: The ▲/▼ marks: show a deviation of a link above N percent of its usual value (5–30, 10 by default)
host_cli.help.dev_spread: The ▲/▼ marks: take the usual spread of the link into account (on by default; off — the percent only)
host_cli.set.bad_dev: The deviation threshold «{value}» is a whole percent from {lo} to {hi}.
host_cli.set.retry_on: If a link drops sharply, I’ll check again in 1–2 h.
host_cli.set.retry_off: The repeat after a sharp drop is off; the repeats waiting are canceled.
host_cli.set.dev_spread: The ▲/▼ marks: a deviation above {pct}% of the usual value and above the usual spread.
host_cli.set.dev_plain: The ▲/▼ marks: a deviation above {pct}% of the usual value.
host_cli.set.preview: It will be so — nothing saved. To save: the same call with code, after the person agrees.
host_cli.set.code_bad: The code does not match: the settings or the change are different now. Look at the change again — without code.
host_cli.help.set_code: The code of a preview: save only the change that was shown
host_cli.help.set_yes: Agree to «much traffic»: turn the repeats on with a heavy schedule without the question
host_cli.set.retry_ask: The repeats after a sharp drop add up to {mb} a day — the schedule already uses much traffic. Turn them on?
host_cli.set.retry_need_yes: Much traffic: the repeats add up to {mb} a day. Add --yes if you agree.
host_cli.set.retry_heavy_dry: Much traffic: the repeats add up to {mb} a day — they turn on only with consent (--yes or the question in a terminal).
host_cli.set.retry_heavy_mcp: Much traffic: the repeats add up to {mb} a day. With such a schedule only a person turns them on — in the server’s terminal: kaskadctl host set --bench-retry on.
